v.note: The SND16 v, re-cut after the owner called it “shouting” beside its neighbour: measured 6.2 dB louder and 400 Hz brighter than the vowel it stands next to. Recipe, from the shipped clip's own body: gain -7 dB, one-pole low-pass at 1800 Hz, re-peaked to -3.5 dBFS, 40 ms fades, then the pack's 80/300 ms padding. Reproduce with tools/build_of_round.py --ship, which refuses unless the bytes match. Every /v/ in the bank takes this clip, not only “of”.

_ship_review_2026_08_12: Ten shipped sounds re-heard side by side, owner's verdicts. short_a BEST; short_e, short_i, short_o, short_u, schwa, long_e, oo_book good; th_this and h POOR. Two things this closed. First: a verdict does not survive a change of context. th_this and h were both graded 'perfect (owner)' in their own rounds and are poor when heard beside their neighbours, so a sound must be judged in the company it will keep, not alone. Second: the owner ruled the same day that schwa 'was the one I think we did the least well' and must not be used as the authority for making new sounds - it had been the target of three failed rounds for the word 'a'. short_a is the reference now, and its entry records no method at all, which is its own fault (docs/open-faults.md).
